subject.title: OpenClawGateway being deleted/rolled back after the failed setup.

question: Should end-user local gateway setup keep transactional rollback as the default after late pairing/configuration failures, or preserve the partially created gateway so users can recover in-product?
rationale: Current code and docs make rollback-on-failure intentional for the UI, but the issue shows that policy can erase a usable created gateway after a late setup failure and leave first-run users without a non-technical recovery path.

options.title: Use stage-aware recovery
options.body: Preserve the gateway after late failures and add visible recovery actions, while still cleaning early unsafe partial installs.

options.title: Keep rollback default
options.body: Retain transactional cleanup for all setup failures and instead improve the failure page with clearer retry/upgrade guidance.

options.title: Make rollback an explicit user choice
options.body: Ask users whether to preserve or remove the local gateway after a failure, trading clarity for another setup decision.

recommendation.title: Use stage-aware recovery
recommendation.body: Preserve the gateway after late failures and add visible recovery actions, while still cleaning early unsafe partial installs.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current setup/pairing follow-up signal from the issue discussion and related merged diagnostic PR.
